# Median full-package task seconds from four complete post-#5350/#5355 hosted
# Build and Test runs on 28 November 2026: 46111828719, 46115225207,
# 46116465436, and 46119500388. Each run observed all 174 ordinary packages
# (internal/config fell from 323.0s to 72.3s and internal/api/configapi from
# 142.8s to 56.5s, while pkg/metrics rose from 260.6s to 324.9s and
# internal/mock from 96.8s to 126.9s). Under leave-one-out holdout validation
# across all four runs, combined 3-way PR peak task-seconds drop by -201.9s to
# -278.0s across all three 3-way PR runs (46111828719, 46116465436, 46119500388)
# and combined 2-way peak task-seconds drop by -112.5s to -183.2s across all
# four runs, separating pkg/metrics, cmd/pulse-agent, and internal/notifications
# one per rest shard.
# Weights schedule the source-listed inventory. New and small packages use
# the mean of the medians below 20 seconds. The release queue runs monitoring
# and installtests whole, so keep their whole-package task-second medians here.
# monitoring-test-seconds.txt and installtests-test-seconds.txt remain unchanged
# because leave-one-out validation confirmed both already outperform reweighted
# alternatives.
DEFAULT_WEIGHT 4.143
# Keep both fixed-slice offset vectors zeroed: monitoring and installtests
# slice weights stay balanced once ordinary package load is balanced across
# shards. Re-measure after hosted runs if fixed slice costs diverge again.
# This is scheduling, not a wall-time claim.
